questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to live in London, as the city and its culture fascinated me. I saw an exchange semester as a unique opportunity to do so.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Goldsmiths was quick to answer any questions and very informative and helpful during the process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a welcome week, where we were given the most crucial information for our upcoming term.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in a dorm room on campus with other Erasmus-exchange students with a private toilet/bathroom. Most of the exchange students did this, which made it easy to connect with other exchange students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a shared kitchen on each floor between 8 residents.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Although it is expensive, you had everything you needed and the support staff was very helpfull with any problems at all hours of the day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process was very easy and straightforward online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were different support teams you could contact, if you had any questions regarding your registration of enrolment.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful. There was a lot of restructuring with classes, which let to a lot of confusion about which classes would be available. I did not know my classes, when the term started.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have any questions, their support staff is very helpful and informative. I never had to wait more than a day for a response.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Due to cancellations of several of my classes, I had to take BA modules to get enough credits/ECTS. The number of MA modules for exchange student was quite limited even beforehand, which made the process even more difficult. The general academic level was not as high as classes at UCPH, but they had some very interesting modules to choose from.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Re-Thinking the International (7,5 ECTS), New Radical Political Economy (7,5 ECTS) and The Structure of Contemporary Political Communication (15 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Re-Thinking the International was very good, but also similar to International Relation classes at UCPH. As the class was very small, there was room for several good debates regarding International Relations.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: As there is no equipment in the kitchen, you had to buy everything you needed, when you arrived.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Travelling around the UK (with train) is very expensive, and I ended up not doing so during my stay.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of opportunities, but I did not enrol in any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were several sport and cultural clubs you could participate in.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you choose not to live on campus, I would recommend signing up for a club to meet other students, as you do not necessarily meet a lot of new people in your classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore different areas in outer-London, as central London is very packed during the weekends. There are several great markets in the suburbs on weekends worth visiting.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is very similar to Danish culture so it wasn't a problem.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The students in England - as well as some of the exchange students - are very young compared to Danish students on average. However, you mainly experienced this in the dorms.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: London has a lot to offer culturally. I had a lot of time to explore museums, which are often free, and attend the theatre during my time there.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It will probably be a struggle to get the classes you want, but Goldsmiths is very helpfull and it will work out eventually. 

London it expensive! Be prepared to pay a lot even for groceries and transport.

There is a great Danish community in London, which is quite unique.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: DJØF has some great events around London throughout the year, which is a good way to meet other Danes (and exchange students) in the city.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and the insights to the English culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being patient with getting my modules, as it was quite a chaotic process. However, it all worked out in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
